tier_justification: Correctness of Roy-Floyd-Warshall transitive closure is textbook and mechanized (Isabelle/HOL AFP entry cited).
plain_claim: For every Boolean relation r on Fin n, the Floyd-Warshall stage warshall r n relates a to b exactly when r has a non-empty path from a to b (warshall_iff_path), and the closure test acyclicB r returns true exactly when no element reaches itself by a non-empty r-path (acyclicB_eq_true_iff). The Decidable instance for Acyclic is defined from acyclicB, so a `decide` verdict on Acyclic is a verdict about the TransGen-based definition.
nonvacuity_witness: The chain 0→1→2 (with 0→2) is acyclic; the 3-cycle and a self-loop are not.
non_claims: Supporting infrastructure: a reference point used to check litmus verdicts by kernel evaluation; it says nothing about memory models.
Says nothing about efficiency beyond kernel evaluation of small instances (n ≤ 8 is used here).
Acyclic is defined via Relation.TransGen; no claim about other cycle notions (e.g. simple cycles of bounded length).

tier_justification: SC ⊆ TSO is standard (both models are instances of the frameworks of Alglave et al.); restated for the toy without well-formedness hypotheses.
plain_claim: Every candidate execution, well-formed or not, that is SC-consistent (po ∪ rf ∪ co ∪ fr acyclic) is TSO-consistent (SC per location, and ppo ∪ rfe ∪ co ∪ fr ∪ fenceOrd acyclic, where ppo and fenceOrd relate memory accesses only).
nonvacuity_witness: The SC outcome of SB (each read sees the other thread's write).
non_claims: This is the inclusion (permissiveness) direction: every SC-consistent execution is TSO-consistent. It does not justify running SC programs unfenced on TSO; that would need the converse, which fails (sb-tso-not-sc).
No well-formedness is assumed. The premise is SC-consistency with fence events present; no claim is made with SCConsistentErased as premise.
Fence events are not endpoints of ppo or fenceOrd, so fence events (and, e.g., a po self-loop on a fence) never lie on a TSO cycle.

Toy model: finite candidate executions of straight-line programs, one access size, no read-modify-write or locked instructions, no registers, dependencies or control flow, a single full fence. These theorems neither establish nor refute the corresponding claims about x86 multiprocessors or the x86-TSO abstract machine; the derived (modeling bridge) claims argue the connection to x86 separately. Nothing is claimed about C11/RC11, Java, out-of-thin-air behaviour, mixed-size accesses, ARM, POWER, RISC-V, or compiler optimisations other than fence insertion.

That TSOConsistent captures x86-TSO is a modeling bridge (derived, not a theorem): it is the two-axiom form (SC per location; acyclic(ppo ∪ rfe ∪ co ∪ fr ∪ fence) with ppo = ([RW];po;[RW]) \ (W×R) and fence = [RW];po;[F];po;[RW]) of Alglave, Maranget and Tautschnig (TOPLAS 2014, Fig. 5 and Fig. 21), whose Lemma 4.1 proves equivalence to SPARC TSO via Alglave (FMSD 2012), Def. 23; no theorem here relates it to the x86-TSO abstract machine or to hardware.

tier_justification: n6 is the published test showing store forwarding on x86 (CACM 2010, Sect. 2.2); TPHOLs 2009 explains that keeping same-address write→read pairs in memory order gives a strictly stronger model (test n7).
plain_claim: Keeping same-location write→read pairs in preserved program order (dropping only different-location write→read pairs) gives a model strictly stronger than TSOConsistent: every execution consistent under the variant is TSOConsistent (tsoConsistent_of_tsoConsistentKeepSameLocWR), and the n6 execution Litmus.n6Weak of n6Prog defined in Litmus.lean (r0 = 1, read from the thread's own x := 1; r1 = 0, the initial y; co on x: initial write, then thread 1's x := 2, then thread 0's x := 1, so final x = 1 and y = 2), a store-forwarding outcome that x86-TSO allows, is well formed and TSOConsistent but rejected by the variant.
nonvacuity_witness: The SB weak outcome is consistent under the variant; n6Weak is an execution of n6Prog.
non_claims: Shows the variant is too strong on one test; does not classify all differences between the two models.

plain_claim: For every straight-line program P and every TSO-consistent candidate execution X of fenceAfterStores P whose rf and co are well formed (RfCoWf: rf from writes to reads of the same location and value, total and functional; co between same-location writes, transitive, total, with initialisation writes first), there is an order-preserving map f from the events of P to the events of X that hits every memory access of X (so it misses only fence events) such that X.comap f, the events, po, rf and co of X read through f, is a well-formed SC-consistent candidate execution of P.

hypotheses.purpose: X is an execution of the compiled program

hypotheses.name: hwf : X.RfCoWf
hypotheses.purpose: well-formedness of rf and co: every Wf conjunct except the four po conditions (implied by hX) and CoIrrefl (implied by SC per location); each conjunct is inherited by the corresponding conjunct of (X.comap f).Wf. The nine conjuncts are not independent once SC per location holds: RfFunctional follows from RfSameLoc, RfKinds and CoTotal (Exec.rfFunctional_of_perLocSC), and CoTrans from CoKinds and CoTotal (Exec.coTrans_of_perLocSC). Tight as a bundle: the counterexample violates RfTotal (a read with no rf source); necessity of the individual conjuncts is not claimed.

nonvacuity_witness: fenceAfterStores sbProg and its SC execution sbFencedSC; with the explicit map sbSrcIdx the source execution is an SC execution of sbProg.
non_claims: Outcome agreement is by construction: the read values, rf and co of X.comap f are those of X at the images of f; no separate observational-equivalence theorem is stated.
The map f is not claimed to be unique (when P has its own mfence next to an inserted one, either fence event may be chosen).
Does not prove completeness: that every SC execution of P is matched by a TSO-consistent execution of fenceAfterStores P is not proved.

RfCoWf is not claimed to be the weakest premise: two of its conjuncts are redundant given PerLocSC (Exec.rfFunctional_of_perLocSC, Exec.coTrans_of_perLocSC), and it also constrains rf and co at the inserted fences, which the source execution never sees (storeFenceExtraRfOnInserted_check: an rf edge into an inserted fence violates RfCoWf while the conclusion still holds). tier_justification: That a program without synchronization operations is data-race free only if it has no conflicting accesses is folklore of the DRF literature (Adve and Hill 1990 identify synchronization explicitly); made precise here for straight-line programs, including the static collapse of fence-based race exemptions.
plain_claim: For every straight-line program P: (i) every conflicting pair of accesses is unordered by hb = (po ∪ rf)⁺ in some well-formed SC-consistent execution of P; hence (ii) every well-formed SC-consistent execution of P orders all its conflicting pairs by hb if and only if P has no conflicting pair at all; (iii) every well-formed SC-consistent execution of P is RaceFree (conflicting accesses hb-ordered or both satisfying NoUnfencedWRIncident) if and only if the static condition P.ConflictsWRFenced holds; and (iv) every such execution is RaceFreeEither (one side suffices) if and only if P.ConflictsWRFencedEither holds.
